Act as a Senior Technical Writer, Principal Software Engineer, Product Manager, and Developer Experience Engineer.

Project: Mortgage Calculator
Repository: wajidalii/mortgage-calculator
Integration branch: dev

Your task is to prepare this project for professional submission to KnowledgeCity's Technology Division as part of its AI-assisted Calculator Web App take-home assignment.

Focus on creating an outstanding GitHub README, capturing real application screenshots, verifying product documentation, and organizing submission materials.

Do not rewrite the application or modify financial calculation logic.

## 1. Understand the project

Before writing anything:

- Read CLAUDE.md, PRD.md, PLAN.md.
- Inspect the entire application and its routes.
- Read app-roles.md, jobs-to-be-done.md, and user-stories.md.
- Review the existing tests.
- Inspect GitHub issues and PRs.
- Identify actually implemented features.
- Identify features that are incomplete or planned.
- Inspect the current README, if any.

Do not describe a feature as implemented unless it works in the current application.

Use the actual code and test results as the source of truth.

## 2. Capture real application screenshots

Start the application locally using the project's documented commands.

Use Playwright or another available browser automation tool to open the running application.

Capture high-quality screenshots of the real application.

Required screenshots:

1. Homepage — Desktop
2. Homepage — Mobile
3. Mortgage Calculator — Desktop
4. Mortgage Calculator — Mobile
5. Monthly Ownership Cost Breakdown
6. Amortization Schedule
7. Side-by-Side Loan Comparison
8. Refinance Calculator
9. ARM Calculator and Hypothetical Rate Information
10. Saved Scenarios, if implemented

Take screenshots at appropriate viewport sizes:

- Desktop: 1440 × 900
- Mobile: 390 × 844
- Comparison: 1440 × 900 or wider if necessary

Requirements:

- Use actual browser screenshots, not generated mockups.
- Display realistic illustrative sample inputs.
- Ensure visible financial results are consistent with the actual calculations.
- Avoid screenshots showing validation errors unless demonstrating error handling.
- Close irrelevant menus and development overlays.
- Ensure no secrets, personal information or browser developer tools are visible.
- Do not manipulate screenshots to hide defects.
- Capture complete relevant sections when the viewport cannot show all content.
- Verify the application has finished rendering before capturing.
- Use descriptive, consistent filenames.

Save screenshots under:

docs/screenshots/

Example names:

homepage-desktop.png
homepage-mobile.png
calculator-desktop.png
calculator-mobile.png
monthly-breakdown.png
amortization.png
loan-comparison.png
refinance.png
arm-calculator.png
saved-scenarios.png

Do not create placeholder images when a feature or browser environment is unavailable. Report the blocker instead.

## 3. Create a professional README.md

Create or substantially improve README.md in the repository root.

The README must be understandable to both technical and nontechnical KnowledgeCity reviewers.

Use the following structure.

### Project title and introduction

Use the product's actual name: Mortgage Calculator.

Write a concise, compelling description explaining that this application helps U.S. homebuyers and homeowners estimate the broader costs of mortgage financing and explore financial tradeoffs.

Explain why this calculator was chosen for the assignment instead of a basic arithmetic calculator.

### Target audience

Describe the three defined user roles:

- First-time homebuyers
- Existing homeowners
- Mortgage and real-estate professionals

Explain their practical problems and how the application addresses them.

### Key features

Document only features that are actually implemented.

Potential capabilities include:

- Fixed-rate mortgage calculations.
- Adjustable-rate mortgage scenarios.
- Loan terms and down payments.
- Monthly ownership estimates.
- Taxes, insurance, PMI and HOA.
- Cash-to-close estimates.
- Amortization schedules.
- Extra-payment simulations.
- Loan comparison.
- Refinance break-even.
- Affordability estimates.
- Saved scenarios.
- Printable reports.

Verify every feature before including it.

Do not list unfinished features as completed.

### Screenshots

Include a visually organized screenshot gallery using relative Markdown image paths.

Show the homepage and main calculator prominently, followed by comparison, amortization, refinance, and other relevant views.

Keep screenshots legible. Avoid embedding an unnecessarily large collection of nearly identical images.

Provide descriptive alt text for accessibility.

All screenshot links must resolve in the repository.

### Technology stack

Document the actual stack and versions where appropriate:

- React
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Tailwind CSS
- React Router
- Vitest
- Biome
- Yarn
- Docker, if supported

Explain major technology choices briefly.

Do not invent libraries or versions.

### Getting started

This is a critical assignment requirement.

A reviewer must be able to clone and run the app locally without:

- Paid services
- Cloud accounts
- API keys
- Private credentials
- An externally hosted backend

Include:

1. Prerequisites and supported Node.js version.
2. Git clone command.
3. Directory navigation.
4. Corepack/Yarn setup if necessary.
5. Exact dependency installation command.
6. Environment configuration, if actually required.
7. Exact development server command.
8. Local URL to open.
9. Production build and local preview commands.

Test these instructions in a clean environment.

If VITE_API_BASE_URL or other variables are required even when no backend is used, investigate whether that requirement can be safely removed or given a harmless local default.

Do not require reviewers to configure an unnecessary API service.

### Testing and verification

Document the actual commands:

- yarn test
- yarn typecheck
- yarn check
- yarn build

Include the verified number of passing tests only if obtained from an actual test run.

Explain what the major test suites cover, including mortgage arithmetic, rounding, amortization, and error handling.

### Financial assumptions and limitations

Clearly explain:

- Results are estimates.
- Not a loan offer or lender quote.
- Illustrative property-tax assumptions.
- Insurance and PMI assumptions.
- ARM hypothetical future-rate modeling.
- Limits of simplified affordability calculations.
- Relevant differences between actual lender requirements and modeled scenarios.

Do not claim regulatory, lender, or financial certification.

### AI-assisted development

Include a transparent section documenting:

- AI coding tool: Claude Code.
- Actual models used, verified from the session records.
- How AI was used for requirements, architecture, implementation, review and testing.
- How the product owner directed and evaluated the work.
- Which parts were manually reviewed.
- Whether any source code was modified manually.

Do not invent model versions or claim all work was AI-generated without verification.

If manual modifications cannot be determined reliably, ask for confirmation instead of asserting there were none.

### Product documentation

Link to the three required documents:

- docs/app-roles.md
- docs/jobs-to-be-done.md
- docs/user-stories.md

If the files already exist elsewhere, preserve their content and organize them consistently.

### AI session transcripts

Explain where full, unmodified session exports are located.

Link to the transcripts/ directory.

These must be genuine complete session exports, not summaries.

### Project structure

Include a concise directory tree of important folders.

Do not list every component or generated file.

### Future improvements

Document meaningful planned features separately from implemented functionality.

### License and contact

Only include a license if the repository actually contains a license or the owner has approved one.

Do not invent contact details.

## 4. Validate the three required product documents

The assignment requires three documents in this order:

1. App Roles
2. Jobs To Be Done
3. User Stories with Acceptance Criteria

Review the existing files against the KnowledgeCity requirements.

### App Roles

Each role must follow the pattern:

"A [role] is [who this person is and their situation]. They can [what they see and do]. They must never [what the app must prevent]."

### Jobs To Be Done

Each job must follow:

"When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome]."

Jobs describe real user needs, not interface elements or application features.

Each job must identify its corresponding role.

### User Stories

Each story must follow:

"As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]."

Each story must:

- Reference a defined job.
- Include testable acceptance criteria.
- Cover relevant normal, invalid and boundary cases.
- Have an accurate status: Implemented or Not implemented.

Do not mark stories implemented simply because code exists or a PR was merged.

Verify the running behavior and acceptance criteria.

Preserve the traceability between roles, jobs and stories.

## 5. Preserve complete AI session transcripts

The assignment explicitly requires complete transcripts from the first AI prompt to the final response.

Inspect available session exports.

Organize the genuine exports under:

transcripts/

Use filenames such as:

session-01.md
session-02.md
session-03.md

Continue numbering for additional sessions.

Requirements:

- Use actual Claude Code exports.
- Do not generate reconstructed transcripts.
- Do not summarize conversations.
- Do not omit unsuccessful attempts or corrected mistakes.
- Preserve the original prompt and response sequence.
- Remove only passwords, API keys, tokens, and other genuinely sensitive secrets.
- Do not make unrelated transcript edits.

If previous session exports are unavailable, identify the missing sessions and report how they can be recovered from Claude Code's local session history.

Do not fabricate missing material.

## 6. Submission readiness verification

Verify that the final project satisfies the KnowledgeCity assignment.

Check:

- Current-browser compatibility.
- Local startup without paid services.
- No required API keys.
- Complete source code.
- No committed node_modules or dist output.
- Valid README instructions.
- Working screenshot paths.
- Genuine AI session transcripts.
- Accurate product documents.
- Testable acceptance criteria.
- Honest story implementation statuses.
- Clear financial errors and boundary handling.
- No exposed credentials.
- All README links work.

Create a concise submission checklist and report any unmet requirements.

Do not claim the submission is ready if a required item is missing.

## 7. GitHub workflow

Follow CLAUDE.md.

1. Fetch the latest dev.
2. Inspect existing open PRs and issues.
3. Check whether README, screenshots or submission documentation is already tracked.
4. Create an appropriate documentation issue only if one does not already exist.
5. Create a dedicated branch from latest dev.
6. Commit only related documentation and screenshot changes.
7. Run relevant checks.
8. Push and open a PR targeting dev.

Do not modify mortgage calculations.
Do not commit directly to main or dev.
Do not merge without my approval.

## 8. Final report

Provide:

- README file summary.
- Screenshot filenames and dimensions.
- Features verified.
- Features omitted because unfinished.
- Product document verification results.
- Transcript inventory and missing sessions.
- Exact tested local startup commands.
- Automated test results.
- Submission readiness checklist.
- GitHub issue and PR links.
- Any outstanding blockers.

The final repository should be easy for a KnowledgeCity reviewer to clone, run, understand, evaluate and discuss during a follow-up interview.

Prioritize accuracy, professionalism, clarity and genuine evidence over impressive-looking but unsupported claims.

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Mortgage Calculator

Web calculator for U.S. home buyers and owners (see `PRD.md`, `user-stories.md`, `app-roles.md`, `jobs-to-be-done.md` for product scope). This repo holds the boilerplate (routing, layout, tooling, Docker) plus the first foundations: integer money/rate primitives, the defaults registry and the shared Disclaimer. Calculator features are tracked as GitHub issues and milestones (see `PLAN.md` section 9).

## Stack

- React 19, React Router 8 (`createBrowserRouter`), TypeScript 7 (strict), Vite 8
- Tailwind CSS 4 via `@tailwindcss/vite`. CSS-first config in `src/styles/index.css`; there is no `tailwind.config.js`
- Biome 2.6 for lint and format; Prettier only for `*.md`, `*.yml`, `*.yaml`
- Yarn 4 (Berry) through Corepack, `nodeLinker: node-modules`. Node >= 22 (`.nvmrc`)
- Husky + lint-staged
- Vitest 5 for tests (co-located `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx` files in `src/`)
- No state library (no Zustand/Redux). `useState` / `useReducer` in feature hooks; Context only for stable global data
- Versions are pinned exactly in `package.json`

## Commands

Use `yarn`, not `npm`. If `yarn` is not found, add `~/.local/bin` to PATH (the Corepack shim lives there; the Husky hook needs it too).

| Command                         | What it does                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `yarn dev`                      | Local dev server (`vite --host`, port 5173). Needs a `.env` (copy `.env.example`)                    |
| `yarn start`                    | Production: `yarn build && serve -s dist -l ${PORT:-3000}`                                           |
| `yarn build`                    | `tsc -b && vite build`                                                                               |
| `yarn typecheck`                | `tsc -b --noEmit`                                                                                    |
| `yarn test` / `yarn test:watch` | Vitest: single run / watch mode. Tests are `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`; the default environment is node |
| `yarn lint` / `yarn lint:fix`   | `biome lint .` / `biome lint --write .`                                                              |
| `yarn check` / `yarn check:fix` | Biome lint + format + import sorting, check / write                                                  |
| `yarn format`                   | Biome format, then Prettier on md/yml/yaml                                                           |

Yarn Berry does not run `pre*`/`post*` hooks on custom scripts (so `start` calls `yarn build` explicitly) and does not run `prepare` (so Husky installs via `postinstall`).

## Layout rule

**Code goes in `src/`. Every config file goes in the repo root.**

```
src/
  main.tsx
  vite-env.d.ts          typed ImportMetaEnv
  app/                   App.tsx, router.tsx, providers.tsx
  layouts/               MainLayout.tsx (AppHeader + Outlet)
  pages/                 HomePage, CalculatorPage, NotFoundPage (one lazy chunk each)
  features/              feature folders: components/ hooks/ types.ts
  components/ui/         Tailwind primitives (Button, Card, segmented-control classes)
  components/layout/     AppHeader (brand + main nav)
  components/feedback/   PageLoader, ErrorBoundary, Disclaimer
  hooks/                 shared hooks (useDebouncedValue, usePrinting, useInView, useFitsViewport)
  services/api/client.ts typed fetch wrapper; only code that touches the network
  config/env.ts          validates VITE_* once at import, throws if missing
  config/defaults/       defaults registry (values with source, as-of date, confidence) and state tax table
  config/disclaimer.ts   PRD section 11 disclaimer text
  lib/                   pure helpers: cn, money (cents), rate (micros), decimal parsing, rounding
  types/units.ts         branded Cents and Micros types
  types/  assets/  styles/index.css
```

`design/` holds the static HTML design reference for the calculator dashboard. It is not app code and is excluded from Biome.

Root configs: `biome.json`, `biome-plugins/`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `.prettierrc`, `.lintstagedrc.json`, `.husky/`, `.yarnrc.yml`, `.env.example`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.dockerignore`, `.claude/agents/`.

## Code conventions (enforced by Biome)

1. **Components are arrow functions** with a **default export**:

   ```tsx
   const Foo = () => { ... };
   export default Foo;
   ```

   No `function Foo()` components, no named component exports, no `export { ... }` in `.tsx` files. Enforced by GritQL plugins in `biome-plugins/`, scoped to `src/**/*.tsx`.

2. **Known gap:** Biome cannot assert that a file _has_ a default export. The rules ban every other way to export a component, but cannot catch a `.tsx` file with no default export, or one that default-exports something other than the component. Check this in review.
3. Every page and the layout are loaded with `lazy()` and must default-export. Do not lazy-load tiny leaf components; that causes request waterfalls and hurts LCP.
4. No `any` (`noExplicitAny` is an error). Use explicit interfaces and `import type` for type-only imports.
5. `ErrorBoundary.tsx` wraps a non-exported class (error boundaries require a class) inside a default-exported arrow component.
6. Non-component `.ts` files (hooks, lib, services, config) may use named exports.
7. Biome style: tabs, double quotes. Run `yarn check:fix` before committing.
8. Performance: keep state as low in the tree as possible, memoize measured hot paths only, defer or debounce heavy recalculation on text input to protect INP.

## Environment variables

- Copy `.env.example` to `.env` for local work. `.env` is gitignored.
- Only `VITE_*` variables are readable by the client, and **every one is inlined into the public bundle**. Never put secrets, tokens or private keys in them.
- Read env only through `src/config/env.ts`, never `import.meta.env` directly elsewhere.
- Current keys: `VITE_API_BASE_URL`, `VITE_APP_NAME`.

## Git workflow

Branches:

| Branch                     | Purpose                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `main`                     | Production releases only. The initial commit goes here                                     |
| `dev`                      | Integration branch. Created from `main` after the initial commit                           |
| `feat/<short-kebab-name>`  | New functionality. Example: `feat/implemented-auth-module`                                 |
| `fix/<short-kebab-name>`   | Bug fixes. Example: `fix/rounding-in-amortization`                                         |
| `chore/<short-kebab-name>` | Tooling, deps, config, docs, refactors with no behavior change. Example: `chore/bump-vite` |

Rules:

- Branch names are `type/kebab-case-description`, with type one of `feat`, `fix`, `chore`.
- All work branches are created **from `dev`** and merged **back into `dev`**. Never branch from or merge feature work directly into `main`.
- `dev` goes to `main` through a **release cycle** (release merge, then tag the release on `main`). No direct commits to `main` or `dev` after the initial commit.
- The pre-commit hook runs lint-staged (Biome on staged files, Prettier on md/yml/yaml) and then `yarn typecheck`. A commit that fails lint or types is rejected. Do not bypass with `--no-verify`.
- The local repo currently has no commits and its default branch is named `master`. Rename it with `git branch -m main` before the initial commit.

## Commit messages

Commit messages are **computed from the actual diff** (`git diff --staged`), never guessed. When asked to commit, read the staged diff first, then write a multi-line message:

```
Feature: Implemented auth module

- Added login and logout routes with lazy-loaded pages
- Added useAuth hook holding session state in a reducer
- Added typed auth calls to the API client
- Updated the router to redirect unauthenticated users
```

Rules:

- **Title:** `<Type>: <Past-tense summary>`, sentence case, no trailing period, about 72 characters or fewer.
- **Type** matches the branch type: `feat/*` -> `Feature`, `fix/*` -> `Fix`, `chore/*` -> `Chore`.
- **Body:** a blank line after the title, then one `- ` bullet per distinct change, each starting with a past-tense verb (Added, Updated, Removed, Fixed, Renamed, Moved). Every bullet must correspond to something in the diff; do not describe changes that are not there.
- Keep bullets specific (name the module, hook, route or config touched) and group trivial edits (formatting, import order) into one bullet.
- One logical change per commit. If the diff mixes unrelated changes, split it into separate commits.
- The initial commit on `main` follows the same format, for example `Chore: Initialized project boilerplate`.

## Docker

No nginx: production serves the built `dist/` with `serve` (SPA fallback on).

- Stages: `deps` -> `dev` | `build` -> `prod-deps` -> `prod`.
- `docker compose --profile dev up --build`: dev server on 5173 with bind mounts (polling enabled for file watching).
- `docker compose --profile prod up --build`: static server on 3000 (`PORT` env), non-root `node` user, health check on.
- `VITE_*` values are inlined at build time, so the prod image takes them as build args (`VITE_API_BASE_URL`, `VITE_APP_NAME`).
- Image builds set `HUSKY=0` because there is no `.git` inside the image. `prod-deps` removes the `postinstall` script from its own copy of `package.json` (the repo's file is untouched).
- If a `public/` directory is added, add a bind mount for it to the compose dev service.
- Yarn is fetched through Corepack at build time, so builds need network access.

## Security

- A CVE baseline was taken on 2026-10-30 by querying OSV.dev, GitHub advisories and NVD for every direct dependency at its pinned version. No known vulnerabilities affected any of them. This is a weak signal: the versions are brand new, so advisories may not exist yet, and NVD was searched by keyword only. Re-run a dependency check before releases and when bumping versions.
- Do not use `npm audit`/`yarn audit` as the only check.
- **Privacy:** user inputs never leave the browser. `src/services/api/client.ts` is the only file that may use `fetch` or other network APIs, and nothing outside `src/services/` may import it. `src/services/networkGuard.test.ts` enforces this (and that `index.html` loads nothing from another origin). Saved scenarios use `localStorage` only. If a real API is ever added on purpose, change that test and the privacy statement in the same PR.

## Open items

- Calculator features from `PRD.md` are not started; only primitives, defaults and the Disclaimer exist. Progress is tracked in GitHub milestones.
- `Providers` (`src/app/providers.tsx`) is a pass-through.
- Closing the default-export lint gap (see Code conventions, item 2) would need a small check script.
