# Jobs to Be Done: Mortgage Ownership Calculator

Source: PRD.md, section 5. Version 0.1 (draft). Date: 2026-10-30.

A job states the situation, the motivation, and the result the user wants. Each job below serves one or more roles. Each job links to the stories that serve it.

## Job format

"When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [expected outcome]."

## J-1 First-Time Buyer: know the full cost

**Role:** AR-1 First-Time Buyer.

**Job:** "When I plan to buy my first home, I want to know the full monthly cost and the cash I need, so I can decide what price I can afford."

**Why this job is hard today**

- Free calculators often show only principal and interest.
- Tax, insurance, PMI, and HOA are easy to forget.
- Cash needed at closing is a separate number that many tools hide.

**Success looks like**

- The user sees one itemized monthly total.
- The user sees what goes to the lender and what is paid elsewhere.
- The user sees the cash to close.
- The user knows which numbers are estimates.

**Stories:** S-1 to S-12, S-15, S-16, S-18

## J-2 Homeowner: decide to change the loan

**Role:** AR-2 Homeowner.

**Job:** "When I think about refinancing or paying extra, I want to see the savings and the break-even point, so I can decide if the change is worth it."

**Why this job is hard today**

- The savings from extra payments are hard to picture.
- A lower rate can still lose money if closing costs are high.
- Users do not know how long it takes to recover the cost.

**Success looks like**

- The user sees the payoff month and the interest saved.
- The user sees the break-even month for a refinance.
- The user sees the assumptions used.

**Stories:** S-1 to S-10, S-13 to S-16, S-18

## J-3 Professional: show tradeoffs to a client

**Role:** AR-3 Professional.

**Job:** "When I advise a client, I want to show the tradeoffs between loans side by side, so the client can decide with clear numbers."

**Why this job is hard today**

- Professionals often use more than one tool for one meeting.
- Results are hard to compare when each is on a different screen.
- A client needs a report to take home.

**Success looks like**

- The user sees two loans in two columns.
- The user changes one input and both columns update.
- The user prints a report that the client can keep.

**Stories:** S-1 to S-10, S-15, S-17 to S-19

## J-4 All roles: trust the numbers

**Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3.

**Job:** "When I see a number, I want to know which inputs are estimates, so I can trust it or correct it."

**Why this job matters**

- Every default in the product is an estimate.
- State-level tax is a coarse estimate. A user can see a different number on a listing site.
- Defaults can become old. A user must be able to see how old they are.

**Success looks like**

- The user sees a label on each value: entered, illustrative, or overridden.
- The user sees the "as of" date and the source of each default.
- The user sees "May be out of date" when a default is more than 365 days old.
- The user can override any default.
- The user sees the disclaimer on every result and every printed page.

**Stories:** S-3, S-4, S-5, S-8, S-9, S-10, S-19

## Job and story map

| Job | R1                            | R2         | R3           | R4           |
| --- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | ------------ |
| J-1 | S-1 to S-10                   | S-11, S-12 | S-15, S-16   | S-18         |
| J-2 | S-1 to S-10                   | None       | S-13 to S-16 | S-18         |
| J-3 | S-1 to S-10                   | None       | S-15         | S-17 to S-19 |
| J-4 | S-3, S-4, S-5, S-8, S-9, S-10 | None       | None         | S-19         |

## Open items

- Q-1 (business model) is not decided. If the model is lead generation, a new job may be needed for the lender or agent who receives the lead. If the model is a paid professional tier, J-3 may split into free and paid parts. See PRD.md, section 13.
# User Stories: Mortgage Ownership Calculator

Source: PRD.md, section 7. Version 0.1 (draft). Date: 2026-10-30.

All story statuses are "Planned". Money in examples is shown in dollars. The product stores cents (decision D-4). Rates are stored as integer millionths (decision D-5).

## How to read this file

- "Serves" links the story to a job in jobs-to-be-done.md.
- "Roles" links the story to a role in app-roles.md.
- Each acceptance criterion uses the Given, When, Then format.
- Numbers in the criteria are test values. They come from the golden cases in PRD.md, section 12.

## Release plan

Each release ships only after the release before it passes all tests. If the schedule slips, drop the latest release first.

| Release         | Content                                                                                                                   | Stories      |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| R1 Core         | Fixed loan, tax, insurance, PMI, HOA, itemized total, amortization, 5/6 ARM, assumptions panel, validation, mobile layout | S-1 to S-10  |
| R2 Buyer        | Closing costs, cash to close, simplified affordability                                                                    | S-11, S-12   |
| R3 Owner        | Extra payments, refinance break-even, rate sensitivity, cost growth                                                       | S-13 to S-16 |
| R4 Professional | Comparison, saved scenarios, print report                                                                                 | S-17 to S-19 |

## R1 Core

### S-1 Enter purchase and loan inputs

**Serves:** J-1, J-2, J-3. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to enter the home price, down payment, loan term, and interest rate, so that I can see the loan amount and the loan-to-value (LTV) ratio."

- Given price $500,000 and down payment 20%, when I view the result, then the loan amount is $400,000 and the LTV is 80.00%.
- Given I change the down payment from a percent to a dollar amount, when I leave the field, then the other form of the value updates to match.
- Given the down payment is 100%, when I view the result, then the loan amount is $0 and the principal and interest is $0.

### S-2 See the fixed monthly principal and interest

**Serves:** J-1, J-2, J-3. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to see the monthly principal and interest for a fixed loan, so that I know the core payment."

- Given loan $400,000, rate 6.50%, and term 30 years, when I calculate, then principal and interest is $2,528.27.
- Given the same loan with a 20 year term, when I calculate, then principal and interest is $2,982.29.
- Given the same loan with a 15 year term, when I calculate, then principal and interest is $3,484.43.
- Given the rate is 0%, when I calculate, then principal and interest is the loan amount divided by the number of payments, rounded to cents.

### S-3 Estimate property tax by state

**Serves:** J-1, J-4. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to pick a state and see an estimated property tax, so that I do not need to look it up first."

- Given price $500,000 and state NJ, when I view the result, then the annual tax is $10,000.00 and the monthly tax is $833.33.
- Given price $500,000 and state TX, when I view the result, then the annual tax is $8,000.00 and the monthly tax is $666.67.
- Given I enter my own annual tax, when I leave the field, then the product uses my value and shows the label "Manual override".
- Given I clear the override, when I leave the field, then the product returns to the state demo rate.
- Given any state is selected, when the tax shows, then the label "Illustrative estimate" is next to it.

### S-4 Enter insurance, HOA, and other monthly costs

**Serves:** J-1, J-4. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to enter insurance, HOA, and other monthly costs, so that the total includes them."

- Given annual insurance $1,800, when I view the result, then monthly insurance is $150.00.
- Given monthly HOA $100, when I view the result, then HOA is $100.00 and it appears in the non-escrow group.
- Given I leave insurance empty, when I view the result, then the product uses the national default ($2,400 per year) and shows the label "Illustrative estimate".
- Given I enter a negative value, when I leave the field, then I see an error and the value is not used.

### S-5 See PMI and when it ends

**Serves:** J-1, J-4. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to see an estimate of PMI and when it ends, so that I know how long I pay it."

- Given price $500,000 and down payment 10%, when I view the result, then the LTV is 90.00% and PMI is on.
- Given the PMI rate 0.50% and loan $450,000, when I view the result, then monthly PMI is $187.50.
- Given price $500,000, down payment 10%, rate 6.50%, and term 30 years, when I view the schedule, then PMI ends in month 109, which is the first month the scheduled balance is at or below 78% of the home price ($390,000).
- Given the same loan, when I view the result, then the product also shows month 95 as the first month the owner can request removal (80% of the home price).
- Given the LTV is exactly 80.00%, when I view the result, then PMI is off.

### S-6 See one itemized monthly estimate

**Serves:** J-1, J-4. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want one itemized monthly estimate, so that I can see what I pay the lender and what I pay elsewhere."

- Given price $500,000, down payment 20%, rate 6.50%, term 30 years, state NJ, annual insurance $1,800, and HOA $100, when I view the result, then I see principal and interest $2,528.27, tax $833.33, insurance $150.00, a lender payment of $3,511.60, HOA $100.00 (non-escrow), and a total of $3,611.60.
- Given any inputs, when the result shows, then the line items add up to the total shown.
- Given PMI is on, when the result shows, then PMI is in the lender payment group.

### S-7 See the amortization schedule

**Serves:** J-1, J-2, J-3. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want a month-by-month amortization schedule, so that I can see interest, principal, and balance over time."

- Given loan $400,000, rate 6.50%, and term 30 years, when I view the schedule, then the lifetime interest is $510,179.81 and the final balance is $0.00.
- Given any fixed loan, when the schedule shows, then the principal paid over the term equals the original loan amount.
- Given I choose the yearly view, when the schedule shows, then each row shows the sum of its 12 months.
- Given tax, insurance, PMI, or HOA, when the schedule shows, then none of them reduce the principal balance.

### S-8 See a 5/6 ARM with true payment recalculation

**Serves:** J-1, J-2, J-3. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to see a 5/6 ARM with a true payment recalculation, so that I understand the risk after the fixed period."

- Given loan $400,000, start rate 6.50%, margin 2.75%, caps 2/1/5, and a flat index of 3.75%, when I view the schedule, then the rate stays 6.50% and the payment stays $2,528.27.
- Given the same loan and an index of 9.00% from month 61, when I view the schedule, then the rates after each reset are 8.50%, 9.50%, 10.50%, then 11.50%, and the first reset payment is $3,015.13.
- Given the same loan and an index of 0.50% from month 61, when I view the schedule, then the rates after each reset are 4.50%, 3.50%, then 3.25%, and the rate never goes below the floor.
- Given a reset, when the product calculates the new payment, then it uses the current balance and the remaining months.
- Given any month after month 60, when the row shows, then the row has the label "Hypothetical rate".

### S-9 See all assumptions in one place

**Serves:** J-4. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want to see all assumptions in one place, so that I know what is real input and what is illustrative."

- Given I open the assumptions panel, when it shows, then it lists every default, its value, and whether it is "Entered", "Illustrative", or "Overridden".
- Given any result screen, when it shows, then the disclaimer text is visible without a click.
- Given a default value, when it shows in the assumptions panel, then the "as of" date and the source name show next to it. Example: "Insurance $2,400 per year. Illustrative. As of 2026-10-30. Source: national averages from four public sources."
- Given the "as of" date of a default is more than 365 days before today, when the panel or the result shows, then the label "May be out of date" shows next to the value.
- Given a printed report, when it prints, then it lists every default used, with its "as of" date.
- Given the user overrides a default, when the panel shows, then the "as of" date is hidden for that value and the label "Overridden" shows.

### S-10 Get clear input checks

**Serves:** J-1, J-2, J-3. **Roles:** AR-1, AR-2, AR-3. **Status:** Planned.

"As a user, I want clear input checks, so that I do not get a wrong result without a warning."

- Given I enter an interest rate above 30% or below 0%, when I leave the field, then I see an error and no result shows.
- Given I enter a down payment greater than the price, when I leave the field, then I see the message "Down payment cannot be more than the price".
- Given I enter text in a money field, when I leave the field, then I see an error and the last valid result stays.
- Given a phone screen width of 360 px, when the page loads, then all inputs and results are usable without sideways scrolling.

**Serves:** J-1. **Roles:** AR-1. **Status:** Planned.

"As a First-Time Buyer, I want to enter closing costs and see the cash to close, so that I know how much money I need on closing day."

**Serves:** J-1. **Roles:** AR-1. **Status:** Planned.

# Accessibility audit

PRD NFR "Accessibility" (issue #32). Audit date: 2026-10-31.

# Mortgage Calculator

A free, no-account web calculator that helps U.S. homebuyers and homeowners estimate **the full cost of a mortgage**, not just the monthly principal and interest, and explore the tradeoffs between loan choices. All calculations run in the browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

![Mortgage Calculator homepage on desktop](docs/screenshots/homepage-desktop.png)

> **Status:** an assignment submission for KnowledgeCity's Technology Division (AI-assisted Calculator Web App). Results are **estimates for planning**. They are not a loan offer, a lender quote or financial advice. See [Financial assumptions and limitations](#financial-assumptions-and-limitations).

## Why a mortgage calculator

A basic arithmetic calculator would have proved very little. A mortgage calculator is a better test of AI-assisted engineering because it needs:

- **Exact money math.** Money is stored as integer cents and rates as integer millionths, so rounding errors cannot build up over a 360-payment schedule.
- **Real product decisions.** Which costs belong in a "monthly payment"? What is paid to the lender and what is paid elsewhere? When does PMI end? What should happen when an input is invalid?
- **Honesty about uncertainty.** Property tax, insurance, PMI and future ARM rates are assumptions. The app labels every one of them as entered, illustrative or overridden.
- **Several connected tools** (purchase, comparison, refinance, extra payments) that share one calculation engine.

## Target audience

The product defines three roles (details in [docs/app-roles.md](docs/app-roles.md)). One product serves all three.

| Role                     | Practical problem                                                                                  | How the app helps                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **First-time buyer**     | Does not know the real monthly cost or the cash needed at closing. Free tools often show only P&I. | One itemized monthly total (lender payment vs. paid elsewhere), PMI, cash to close, and a simplified affordability check.     |
| **Existing homeowner**   | Wonders whether extra payments or a refinance are worth it, and how long it takes to recover costs. | Extra-payment simulation (payoff month, interest saved), refinance break-even, and rate sensitivity.                          |
| **Mortgage / real-estate professional** | Needs to show tradeoffs to a client and hand over a report.                          | Side-by-side loan comparison (fixed vs. fixed, or fixed vs. ARM), saved scenarios and a printable report with the disclaimer. |

## Key features

Every feature below was checked in the running app (see [Testing and verification](#testing-and-verification) and the Verification section of [docs/user-stories.md](docs/user-stories.md)).

- **Purchase inputs.** Home price, down payment as percent or dollars (the two stay in sync), interest rate, and 15, 20 or 30 year terms. Shows loan amount and loan-to-value.
- **Fixed-rate principal and interest**, with the lifetime interest total.
- **5/6 adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM).** Margin, caps and floor, with a true payment recalculation at each reset from the current balance and remaining months. Three assumed index paths (flat, +1 point per year, shock). Rows after the fixed period are labelled **"Hypothetical rate"**.
- **Monthly ownership estimate.** Principal and interest, property tax, homeowners insurance, extra insurance, HOA and other costs, split into _lender payment (escrow)_ and _non-escrow_.
- **Property tax by state.** An illustrative demo rate for a small set of states, with a manual override.
- **PMI.** Estimated when the down payment is under 20%, with the first month you can request removal (80% of the home price) and the month it ends (78%).
- **Closing costs and cash to close.**
- **Simplified affordability.** Front-end and back-end debt-to-income ratios against editable guideline limits (default 28% and 36%), always with a "not a loan approval" statement.
- **Amortization schedule.** Monthly or yearly view, plus a balance chart you can explore by year.
- **Extra payments.** A monthly extra amount or a one-time lump sum, with payoff month and interest saved.
- **Rate sensitivity.** Payment at five nearby rates.
- **Cost growth.** Yearly growth assumptions for property tax and insurance.
- **Assumptions panel.** Every default with its value, source, "as of" date and label, and a "May be out of date" flag after 365 days.
- **Loan comparison** (`/compare`). Two loans side by side, each with its own inputs, plus a "differences at a glance" summary. Swap loans, or copy Loan A to Loan B.
- **Refinance break-even** (`/refinance`). Monthly saving and months to break even. Shows "No monthly saving" instead of a misleading result.
- **Saved scenarios.** Saved in this browser's `localStorage` only, with open and delete (with confirmation). If storage is blocked, the app says so and keeps working.
- **Printable report.** Inputs, itemized estimate, schedule summary, assumptions with "as of" dates, and the disclaimer. Navigation and input controls are hidden when printing.
- **Input validation** with clear messages (for example "Down payment cannot be more than the price"), and a layout that works at 360 px wide.

## Screenshots

All screenshots are real captures of the running app with illustrative sample inputs (a $450,000 home, 20% down, 6.75% rate unless noted).

### Homepage and calculator

| Homepage (desktop, 1440 × 900) | Homepage (mobile, 390 × 844) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Homepage hero and example monthly cost on desktop](docs/screenshots/homepage-desktop.png) | ![Homepage hero on a phone-sized screen](docs/screenshots/homepage-mobile.png) |

| Calculator (desktop, 1440 × 900) | Calculator (mobile, 390 × 844) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Calculator with mortgage inputs on the left and the live monthly cost on the right](docs/screenshots/calculator-desktop.png) | ![Calculator on a phone-sized screen with a sticky monthly cost bar](docs/screenshots/calculator-mobile.png) |

### Monthly ownership cost breakdown

![Itemized monthly cost: principal and interest, property tax and insurance in the lender payment, HOA and other costs outside escrow](docs/screenshots/monthly-breakdown.png)

### Amortization schedule

![Yearly amortization schedule showing payment, principal, interest and balance](docs/screenshots/amortization.png)

### Side-by-side loan comparison

A 15-year loan at 6.00% against a 30-year loan at 6.75% on the same $450,000 home.

![Two loans side by side with a differences-at-a-glance summary](docs/screenshots/loan-comparison.png)

### Refinance break-even

![Refinance calculator showing a 31 month break-even and the monthly saving](docs/screenshots/refinance.png)

### 5/6 ARM and hypothetical rates

![5/6 ARM inputs: margin, caps, floor and index path, with the reset risk warning](docs/screenshots/arm-calculator.png)

![Balance chart with the hypothetical-rate period shaded, and schedule rows labelled Hypothetical rate](docs/screenshots/arm-hypothetical-rates.png)

### Saved scenarios

![A saved scenario listed with Open and Delete buttons](docs/screenshots/saved-scenarios.png)

The mobile screenshots are captured at a 390 × 844 viewport with a 2× pixel ratio (780 × 1688 files). The desktop images that are not 900 px tall are full sections of the page.

## Technology stack

| Area       | Choice (exact version in `package.json`)          | Why                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| UI         | React 19.3.1                                      | Component model fits many small calculators that share logic.                            |
| Language   | TypeScript 7.0.2 (strict)                         | Branded `Cents` and `Micros` types stop money and rates being mixed up at compile time.  |
| Build      | Vite 8.3.5                                        | Fast dev server, small production bundle, lazy-loaded pages.                             |
| Styling    | Tailwind CSS 4.3.3 (CSS-first config)             | Consistent design tokens, no unused CSS shipped.                                         |
| Routing    | React Router 8.5.1                                | Each page is its own lazy chunk.                                                         |
| Tests      | Vitest 5.0.5, Testing Library, jsdom              | Fast unit tests for the maths and component tests for behaviour.                         |
| Lint/format| Biome 2.6.4 (Prettier for Markdown/YAML only)     | One fast tool, with custom rules that enforce the component style in CLAUDE.md.          |
| Packages   | Yarn 4 (Berry) via Corepack                       | Reproducible installs from `yarn.lock`.                                                  |
| Container  | Docker (`Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`)       | Optional. Serves the built app with `serve`; no nginx.                                   |
| CI         | GitHub Actions                                    | Runs check, typecheck, test and build on every pull request.                             |

There is **no backend, database, state library or third-party API**. State lives in `useState` / `useReducer` inside feature hooks.

## Getting started

You do **not** need a paid service, a cloud account, an API key, credentials or a hosted backend. No `.env` file is needed.

**Prerequisites**

- Node.js 22 or newer (`.nvmrc` pins 22).
- Git.
- Corepack (ships with Node) to provide Yarn 4. If `yarn` is not found, run `corepack enable`. If that is not permitted, use `corepack yarn` instead of `yarn` in the commands below.

**Run the app**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/wajidalii/mortgage-calculator.git
cd mortgage-calculator
corepack enable
yarn install
yarn dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>.

**Production build and local preview**

```bash
yarn build     # type-checks, then builds to dist/
yarn start     # builds, then serves dist/ with SPA fallback on http://localhost:3000
```

**With Docker (optional)**

```bash
docker compose --profile dev up --build    # dev server on http://localhost:5173
docker compose --profile prod up --build   # production build on http://localhost:3000
```

**Configuration.** Two optional variables exist, `VITE_APP_NAME` (default "Mortgage Calculator") and `VITE_API_BASE_URL` (default `/api`, currently unused because the app makes no network calls). See `.env.example`. Every `VITE_*` value is inlined into the public bundle, so never put secrets in them.

## Testing and verification

```bash
yarn test        # Vitest, single run
yarn typecheck   # tsc -b --noEmit
yarn check       # Biome lint + format + import order
yarn build       # tsc -b && vite build
```

Result of the most recent run, from a fresh clone-style copy with `yarn install --immutable` and **no `.env`**: **39 test files, 460 tests, all passing**. `yarn typecheck`, `yarn check` and `yarn build` also passed.

The major suites cover:

- **Money and rate arithmetic** (`lib/money`, `lib/rate`, `lib/payment`): integer cents and millionths, rounding, parsing and formatting, including negative amounts and malformed thousands separators.
- **Amortization** (`lib/amortization`, plus a randomized reference-ledger test): principal repaid equals the loan, final balance is exactly $0, yearly rows equal the sum of their months.
- **ARM** (`lib/arm`, `armSchedule`): reset payments from the current balance, caps and floor, and the "Hypothetical rate" label.
- **Product rules:** property tax, PMI and its end months, closing costs, affordability, extra payments, cost growth, rate sensitivity, refinance, comparison and defaults.
- **Error handling and boundaries:** validation messages, 0% rate, 100% down payment, rates above 30% or below 0%, text in money fields, and storage that is blocked.
- **UI behaviour:** calculator, assumptions panel, saved scenarios, compare, refinance and homepage components.
- **Privacy guard** (`services/networkGuard.test.ts`): fails if any code outside `src/services/` can reach the network, or if `index.html` loads anything from another origin.

The acceptance criteria in [docs/user-stories.md](docs/user-stories.md) were also checked by hand-driven browser automation against the running app. The same sample values appear in the tests.

## Financial assumptions and limitations

- **Estimates only.** Results are for planning. They are not a loan offer, a lender quote, a pre-approval or financial advice. The app shows this disclaimer on every result and every printed page.
- **Property tax** uses an **illustrative flat demo rate** for each of a few states, applied to the home price. Real tax depends on county, assessed value and exemptions. You can override it. The demo rates have not yet been checked against a primary source (open issue #29).
- **Homeowners insurance** defaults to an illustrative national average ($2,400 a year). Flood, wind and similar cover is not added automatically. Enter it yourself.
- **PMI** uses an illustrative annual rate on the original loan amount. It is modelled to end at 78% of the home price, and removal can be requested at 80%. Real PMI depends on credit score, loan program and insurer (default not yet replaced with a current insurer figure, issue #27).
- **ARM.** Only a 5/6 ARM is modelled. After the fixed period the rate follows an **assumed** index path (flat, +1 point per year or shock) plus margin, within the caps and floor you enter. These are what-if scenarios, not forecasts, and every such row is labelled "Hypothetical rate". The default margin and caps have not yet been checked against a current Loan Estimate (issue #28).
- **Affordability** is a simplified debt-to-income check against guideline limits. Lenders also look at credit, assets, reserves, loan program rules and more.
- **Refinance** assumes the new loan has the same term as the remaining term and that the costs you enter are paid up front. It ignores taxes, cash-out and the time value of money.
- **Out of scope:** ZIP or address tax lookup, transfer and recording taxes, agent and lender fee estimates, FHA, VA and jumbo rules, user accounts and server storage.

This project makes no claim of regulatory, lender or financial certification.

## AI-assisted development

This project was built with **Claude Code** (Anthropic's CLI coding agent). Details below come from the session exports in [`transcripts/`](transcripts/) and the repository history.

- **Tool and model.** Each of the nine exported sessions opens with the header `Claude Code v2.1.314 · Sonnet 5.5`, so **Sonnet 5.5** was the model for all recorded sessions. The planning session recommended switching to Opus 5.5 for orchestration, but the exports do not show a model switch.
- **Requirements.** Session 01 is a product-management dialogue where Claude acted as a critical product partner and asked one question at a time. It led to the PRD, roles, jobs and user stories.
- **Architecture.** Session 02 produced the stack decisions, project layout, lint rules, Docker setup and the feature roadmap (`PLAN.md`), plus a dependency vulnerability check.
- **Implementation.** Later sessions built the calculation engine and features issue by issue, each on its own branch and pull request, then redesigned the calculator, homepage and compare pages and added motion.
- **Review and testing.** Features were written with tests, and accessibility, performance and privacy audits were run and recorded in `ACCESSIBILITY.md`, `PERFORMANCE.md` and the network-guard test.
- **Product owner direction.** The repository owner set the goals, answered the product questions, approved decisions and design directions, and merged every pull request (all 40 merged PRs were merged by the owner's GitHub account).
- **Manual code changes.** The session exports do not record whether the owner edited any source file by hand, so this README does not claim either way. Git history shows the commits under the owner's git identity (plus a few under the name "Claude" from automated worktree runs).

## Product documentation

The three required documents, in order:

1. [App Roles](docs/app-roles.md) (AR-1 to AR-3)
2. [Jobs To Be Done](docs/jobs-to-be-done.md) (J-1 to J-4)
3. [User Stories with Acceptance Criteria](docs/user-stories.md) (S-1 to S-19, each with a status of Implemented or Not implemented)

Roles, jobs and stories are linked by ID, so each story traces to a job and a role. Wider context: [PRD.md](PRD.md) (scope, rules, test plan), [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) (architecture and roadmap).

## AI session transcripts

Complete, unmodified Claude Code session exports, in order, are in [`transcripts/`](transcripts/): `session-01.md` to `session-09.md`. They run from the first prompt (product discovery) to the Compare Loans redesign (PR #85).

## Project structure

```
src/
  app/            router and providers
  layouts/        main layout (header + page outlet)
  pages/          one lazy-loaded page per route
  features/
    calculator/   inputs, results, ARM, PMI, tax, schedule, assumptions
    compare/      side-by-side loan comparison
    refinance/    break-even calculator
    scenarios/    saved scenarios (localStorage)
    home/         landing page sections
  components/     shared UI, layout and feedback (Disclaimer, ErrorBoundary)
  lib/            pure helpers: money (cents), rate (micros), payment, amortization, ARM
  config/         env defaults, defaults registry, state tax table, disclaimer text
  services/       the only place network code may live (currently unused)
docs/             product documents and design screenshots
transcripts/      full AI session exports
design/           static HTML design reference (not app code)
```

Other root files: `CLAUDE.md` (engineering rules), `PRD.md`, `PLAN.md`, `ACCESSIBILITY.md`, `PERFORMANCE.md`, `MOTION.md`.

## Future improvements

Not implemented yet:

- Verify the five demo state tax rates, the PMI default and the ARM margin and caps against primary sources (issues #29, #27, #28).
- More states and county-level tax lookup.
- Other loan types (FHA, VA, jumbo) and other ARM structures.
- Estimated closing costs and transfer taxes (today the user enters them).
- Decide the business model and success metric (issue #30).
- Exporting a report to PDF or file (today the report is printed from the browser).

## License and contact

No license file has been added to this repository, so no open-source license is granted. Questions about the project can go through the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/wajidalii/mortgage-calculator).

# Mortgage Calculator

A free, no-account web calculator that helps U.S. homebuyers and homeowners estimate **the full cost of a mortgage**, not just the monthly principal and interest, and explore the tradeoffs between loan choices. All calculations run in the browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

![Mortgage Calculator homepage on desktop](docs/screenshots/homepage-desktop.png)

> **Status:** an assignment submission for KnowledgeCity's Technology Division (AI-assisted Calculator Web App). Results are **estimates for planning**. They are not a loan offer, a lender quote or financial advice. See [Financial assumptions and limitations](#financial-assumptions-and-limitations).

## Why a mortgage calculator

A basic arithmetic calculator would have proved very little. A mortgage calculator is a better test of AI-assisted engineering because it needs:

- **Exact money math.** Money is stored as integer cents and rates as integer millionths, so rounding errors cannot build up over a 360-payment schedule.
- **Real product decisions.** Which costs belong in a "monthly payment"? What is paid to the lender and what is paid elsewhere? When does PMI end? What should happen when an input is invalid?
- **Honesty about uncertainty.** Property tax, insurance, PMI and future ARM rates are assumptions. The app labels every one of them as entered, illustrative or overridden.
- **Several connected tools** (purchase, comparison, refinance, extra payments) that share one calculation engine.

## Target audience

The product defines three roles (details in [docs/app-roles.md](docs/app-roles.md)). One product serves all three.

| Role                     | Practical problem                                                                                  | How the app helps                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **First-time buyer**     | Does not know the real monthly cost or the cash needed at closing. Free tools often show only P&I. | One itemized monthly total (lender payment vs. paid elsewhere), PMI, cash to close, and a simplified affordability check.     |
| **Existing homeowner**   | Wonders whether extra payments or a refinance are worth it, and how long it takes to recover costs. | Extra-payment simulation (payoff month, interest saved), refinance break-even, and rate sensitivity.                          |
| **Mortgage / real-estate professional** | Needs to show tradeoffs to a client and hand over a report.                          | Side-by-side loan comparison (fixed vs. fixed, or fixed vs. ARM), saved scenarios and a printable report with the disclaimer. |

## Key features

Every feature below was checked in the running app (see [Testing and verification](#testing-and-verification) and the Verification section of [docs/user-stories.md](docs/user-stories.md)).

- **Purchase inputs.** Home price, down payment as percent or dollars (the two stay in sync), interest rate, and 15, 20 or 30 year terms. Shows loan amount and loan-to-value.
- **Fixed-rate principal and interest**, with the lifetime interest total.
- **5/6 adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM).** Margin, caps and floor, with a true payment recalculation at each reset from the current balance and remaining months. Three assumed index paths (flat, +1 point per year, shock). Rows after the fixed period are labelled **"Hypothetical rate"**.
- **Monthly ownership estimate.** Principal and interest, property tax, homeowners insurance, extra insurance, HOA and other costs, split into _lender payment (escrow)_ and _non-escrow_.
- **Property tax by state.** An illustrative demo rate for a small set of states, with a manual override.
- **PMI.** Estimated when the down payment is under 20%, with the first month you can request removal (80% of the home price) and the month it ends (78%).
- **Closing costs and cash to close.**
- **Simplified affordability.** Front-end and back-end debt-to-income ratios against editable guideline limits (default 28% and 36%), always with a "not a loan approval" statement.
- **Amortization schedule.** Monthly or yearly view, plus a balance chart you can explore by year.
- **Extra payments.** A monthly extra amount or a one-time lump sum, with payoff month and interest saved.
- **Rate sensitivity.** Payment at five nearby rates.
- **Cost growth.** Yearly growth assumptions for property tax and insurance.
- **Assumptions panel.** Every default with its value, source, "as of" date and label, and a "May be out of date" flag after 365 days.
- **Loan comparison** (`/compare`). Two loans side by side, each with its own inputs, plus a "differences at a glance" summary. Swap loans, or copy Loan A to Loan B.
- **Refinance break-even** (`/refinance`). Monthly saving and months to break even. Shows "No monthly saving" instead of a misleading result.
- **Saved scenarios.** Saved in this browser's `localStorage` only, with open and delete (with confirmation). If storage is blocked, the app says so and keeps working.
- **Printable report.** Inputs, itemized estimate, schedule summary, assumptions with "as of" dates, and the disclaimer. Navigation and input controls are hidden when printing.
- **Input validation** with clear messages (for example "Down payment cannot be more than the price"), and a layout that works at 360 px wide.

All screenshots are real captures of the running app with illustrative sample inputs (a $450,000 home, 20% down, 6.75% rate unless noted).

### Homepage and calculator

| Homepage (desktop, 1440 × 900) | Homepage (mobile, 390 × 844) |
| --- | --- |

### Amortization schedule

A 15-year loan at 6.00% against a 30-year loan at 6.75% on the same $450,000 home.

content.text:
The submission prep is done and PR #87 is open against `dev`, but I wouldn't call the project ready to submit yet because two required items are still open.

- **Issue:** https://github.com/wajidalii/mortgage-calculator/issues/86
- **PR:** https://github.com/wajidalii/mortgage-calculator/pull/87 (not merged)

## Two things need you before submitting
1. **Last transcript missing.** `transcripts/` has sessions 01–09, up to PR #85. This session, which produced the README and PR, isn't exported yet. Export it into `transcripts/session-10.md` after we finish.
2. **Manual code edits.** The exports don't show whether you edited any source file by hand. The README states that plainly instead of claiming either way. Tell me and I'll update the line. Three commits in git history are authored as "Claude" rather than you.

## What was done
- **README:** all the requested sections, written from checked behaviour only. Unfinished items sit under Future improvements.
- **Screenshots:** 11 real captures in `docs/screenshots/`, all taken at 1440 × 900 or 390 × 844.
  - Desktop images that aren't 900 px tall (`monthly-breakdown`, `amortization`, `saved-scenarios`) are element crops. The ARM, ARM hypothetical-rates and comparison images are 1440 wide with heights from 572 to 1620.
  - The mobile files are 780 × 1688, because I captured at 2× pixel ratio.
  - The amortization table crop cuts off its last row, because the app scrolls that table internally.
- **No `.env` needed:** `VITE_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_APP_NAME` now have defaults in `src/config/env.ts`. The app never calls its API client. No calculation logic was touched.
- **Product docs:**
  - **Moved:** `app-roles.md`, `jobs-to-be-done.md` and `user-stories.md` now live in `docs/`.
  - **Roles:** each role has the required one-sentence "is / can / must never" form.
  - **Stories:** each story names one role in its sentence.
  - **Statuses:** all 19 stories were all marked "Planned". I checked the criteria in a real browser, and all 19 are now Implemented. Details are in a new Verification section at the end of `docs/user-stories.md`.
  - **S-17 corrected:** it said changing one input updates both loans. The redesigned Compare page gives each loan its own inputs, so I corrected S-17, J-3 and AR-3 to match.
- **Transcripts:** the 9 exports are committed byte-for-byte (sizes match the originals). I added `transcripts/` to `.prettierignore`, because the pre-commit hook would otherwise have rewritten them. A search found no secrets.
- **Models:** every exported session header says Sonnet 5.5. The plan recommended Opus 5.5, but no model switch appears in the exports.

## Test results
From a fresh copy with `yarn install --immutable` and no `.env`:
- `yarn test`: 39 files, 460 tests, all passing
- `yarn typecheck`, `yarn check` and `yarn build`: pass
- The dev server started and served `/calculator`, with no console errors beyond a single 404, which I didn't trace.

## Smaller things
- **Docker:** `yarn dev`, `yarn build` and `yarn start` were run; the Docker commands in the README come from `CLAUDE.md` and weren't rebuilt here.
- **Licence:** the repo has none, and I didn't add one.
- **Open data issues:** #27, #28 and #29 (PMI default, ARM caps and demo tax rates not yet verified) are listed as limitations in the README.
- **Commit message:** the screenshots ended up in the "Moved the product documents" commit, whose message doesn't mention them. I noted this in the PR rather than force-pushing.
- **Leftover stash:** my own redundant `stash@{0}` is still there, because dropping it was blocked. It's safe to drop. `stash@{1}` was already there.

## Add this record in Cloudflare
| Type | Name | Target | Proxy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CNAME | `arm` | `cname.vercel-dns.com` | **DNS only** (grey cloud) |

Keep it grey-cloud at first, because Vercel needs to issue the TLS certificate. Once it's issued you can switch to proxied if you want, with SSL/TLS mode set to Full (strict). Check it with `vercel domains inspect arm.wajidali.dev`. Vercel may show a different target in its dashboard, and if so use that one.

- **`.gitignore` (modified):** the Vercel CLI added `.vercel` and `.env*`.

I didn't commit either, since `main` takes no direct commits. If you want future Git-triggered deploys to keep the SPA routing, I can put both on a `chore/vercel-config` branch and open a PR to `dev`. Without `vercel.json`, a Git-based deploy would 404 on direct visits to `/compare` and `/refinance`.

Auto-deploy from `main` is set up, and PR #89 is open against `dev`: https://github.com/wajidalii/mortgage-calculator/pull/89. I haven't merged it, and nothing has actually auto-deployed yet.

- **Auto-deploy:** the Vercel project `mortgage-calculator` is connected to `wajidalii/mortgage-calculator`. A push to `main` should deploy to production, and other branches should get preview deployments. The connect command reported the repo was already connected. I haven't triggered a push to `main` to confirm the deploy.
- **`HUSKY=0`:** set as a Vercel env var for Production and Preview, so installs on Vercel skip the Git hooks. Vercel stores it as a secret, so it shows as hidden.
- **In the PR:** `vercel.json` (the route rewrite that makes `/compare` and `/refinance` work on direct visits) and the two `.gitignore` lines for the Vercel CLI's local files.

Three things to know:
- **Production deploys wait on your merges.** The Vercel config is only on `dev`/PR #89 for now. Once you merge #89 into `dev` and release `dev` to `main`, the next push to `main` will carry `vercel.json`. Until then, a Git-triggered production deploy would 404 on direct visits to `/compare`. The deploy I made earlier from the CLI already includes it.
- **The domain isn't live yet.** `arm.wajidali.dev` still needs the Cloudflare record: CNAME, name `arm`, target `cname.vercel-dns.com`, DNS only.
- **Local state.** I'm on the `chore/vercel-auto-deploy` branch now. The Vercel CLI also wrote a local `.env.local`, which is gitignored and not committed.
